depth_first_rationale: In the second turn the customer bundles two requests ('dispute and replace. both'), but subsequently follows a sequential, depth-first pattern for all remaining concerns.
uncertainty_rationale: In a certain-fraud scenario the customer's assertive 'yes, 100%. didn't authorize it' is appropriately confident without sounding robotic or over-hedged.
info_drip_rationale: The very first customer turn volunteers all three key facts — merchant (Apple Store), amount ($1,249), and date (Aug 19) — simultaneously without any prompting from the agent.
pragmatic_rationale: Turns like 'yeah expedite it' and 'i'll get the provisional credit while investigation runs right' sound like genuine, colloquial caller speech rather than scripted phrasing.
persona_score_rationale: The terse, expert, calm persona is strongly sustained throughout — single-word or short-phrase answers, knowledgeable use of 'provisional credit' and awareness of the investigation timeline, and zero emotional escalation.
persona_rationale: The customer's closing 'good. that's all' exemplifies the terse, calm, expert persona — no pleasantries, no confusion, just efficient closure.
standout_issue: Front-loading all three key facts (merchant, amount, date) in the opening message is the most unrealistic element; a real caller would typically state the problem first and supply details when asked.
standout_quality: The colloquial, fragmented syntax throughout ('dispute and replace. both', 'yeah expedite it', 'good. that's all') is highly convincing of a real terse caller.
